rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Our Lord is God” followed by steadfastness means affirming God's oneness and lordship, remaining firm without returning to shirk, and acting accordingly.
rows.anchor: Yani Allah’ın vahdâniyet ve rubûbiyetini tasdik ve ikrar edip şirke rücû etmeksizin o ikrarda sâbit olarak muktezâsınca gittiler.

rows.speaker: Tefsîr-i Keşşâf
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf reads thumma as marking the higher, subsequent achievement of steadfastness after confession, since steadfastness is the central matter; it compares 49:15 and means persevering in confession and its demands.
rows.anchor: Tefsîr-i Keşşâf’ta der ki: “ثُمَّ ‘istikāmet’in [4200] mertebede ‘ikrar’dan terâhîsi ve onun üzerine fazlı hasebiyledir. Çünkü bütün şan, istikāmettedir.

rows.speaker: Ebû Bekir
rows.claim: Abu Bakr explains steadfastness as being steadfast in deeds just as in speech.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ebû Bekir’den bir rivayette, kavilde müstakīm oldukları gibi fiilde de müstakīm oldular.

rows.speaker: Ebû Bekr-i Sıddık
rows.claim: In another report, Abu Bakr rejects defining steadfastness as never sinning as too demanding; he says it means not returning to idol worship.
rows.anchor: Ebû Bekr-i Sıddık radıyallahu anh bunu tilâvet edip ‘ne dersiniz?’ dedi, ‘günah işlemediler’ dediler, ‘pek zoruna hamlettiniz, ibâdet-i evsâna dönmediler’ dedi.

rows.speaker: Ömer
rows.claim: Umar says they remained steadfast in obeying God and did not turn to fox-like trickery.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ömer radıyallahu anh da bir hutbesinde bu âyeti tefsir edip demiştir ki: ‘Allah’a itaatte istikāmet yaptılar, tilkiler gibi hîlekârlığa sapmadılar.’

rows.speaker: Osman
rows.claim: Uthman explains steadfastness as sincerity in action.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Osman radıyallahu anh’tan: ‘Amelde ihlâs yaptılar.’

rows.speaker: Ali
rows.claim: Ali explains steadfastness as fulfilling the obligatory duties.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ali kerremallahu vechehu’dan: ‘Ferâizi eda ettiler.’

rows.speaker: Süfyân-ı Sevrî
rows.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri says they acted in accordance with what they had said.
rows.anchor: Süfyân-ı Sevrî hazretlerinden: “Dediklerine muvâfık amel ettiler.”

rows.speaker: Rebî‘ b. Enes
rows.claim: Rabi ibn Anas says they turned away from everything besides God.
rows.anchor: Rebî‘b. Enes’ten: “Allah’ın mâsivâsından i‘râz eylediler”.

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: Sufyan b. Abdullah al-Thaqafi asked for a command to hold to, and the Prophet told him to say “My Lord is God” and then remain upright.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah buyurdu ki: «قُلْ «رَب ِّيَ االلهُ ثُ َّم اسْتَقِمُ

rows.speaker: Resûl-i Ekrem
rows.claim: When Sufyan b. Abdullah asked what the Prophet most feared for him, the Prophet held his tongue and identified it as the danger.
rows.anchor: Resûl-i Ekrem sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem[^5] kendi dilini tutup ‘işte bu’ buyurdu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels descend repeatedly on the steadfast as God's messengers, just as devils accompany disbelievers.
rows.anchor: elçileri melekler iner kâfirlere şeytanlar karîn olduğu gibi bunlara da melekler iner.

rows.speaker: Mücâhid ve Süddî
rows.claim: Mujahid and Suddi place the angels' descent at the time of death.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid ve Süddî demişler: inde’l-mevt

rows.speaker: Mukātil
rows.claim: Muqatil places the angels' descent at the resurrection.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid ve Süddî demişler: inde’l-mevt,[^8] Mukātil demiş: inde’l-ba‘s.

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some say the descent occurs at death, in the grave, and at resurrection.
rows.anchor: Bazıları da hem mevt, hem kabir, hem ba‘s sırası demişler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is unrestricted and also applies to every moment of worldly life.
rows.anchor: Dünyada hayâtın her lahzasına da[^11] sâdıktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect form conveys continuity, while the reflexive form conveys repeated, successive descent; the wording explicitly covers this life and the hereafter.
rows.anchor: تَتَنَزَّلُ hem[^12] muzâri‘olmakla istimrar, hem tefe‘‘ulden olmakla tekellüf ve tevâlî[^13] ifade eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels' command means not to fear what lies ahead or grieve over the past, echoing the description of God's friends in 10:62.
rows.anchor: korkmayın istikbalden [4201] endişe etmeyin {وَلَا تَحْزَنُوا۟} mahzun da olmayın yani geçmişe de merak etmeyin.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels say they are the believers' friends in worldly life and the hereafter, and this wording shows that their descent spans both.
rows.anchor: {نَحْنُ أَوْلِيَآؤُكُمْ} biz sizin evliyânız dostlarınızız

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some take “we are your friends” as direct divine speech, meaning God is the believers' patron, benefactor, protector, and guardian, as in 2:257.
rows.anchor: Ancak bazıları bunun doğrudan doğru kelâm-i ilâhi olduğuna kāil olmuşlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading is that the words are spoken by the angels.
rows.anchor: Lâkin zâhir olan melâikenin kelâmından olmasıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Paradise, believers will have whatever their souls desire.
rows.anchor: canlarınız ne arzu ederse var

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever they ask for there will arrive as soon as they ask.
rows.anchor: hem orada size ne isterseniz var, yani her neyi gelsin derseniz hemen gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised Paradise is received as a guest's welcome and gift from the All-Forgiving, All-Merciful.
rows.anchor: bir nüzül, yani konukluk ikramiye olarak {مِّنْ غَفُورٍۢ رَّحِيمٍۢ} bir Gafûr-i Rahîm’den.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Happiness has two degrees: acquiring excellent qualities perfected in oneself, then going beyond this by working to perfect deficiencies; the passage signals the first and then the second.
rows.anchor: Tam saadet, zatında kâmil olacak sıfât-ı fâzıla iktisab etmektir. Bu dereceyi geçip de nâkısları kemâle erdirmek için çalışmak da fevka’t-tamdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that calamities come from people's deeds addresses sinners; the righteous may also suffer trials to gain reward or higher rank, as in 2:155.
rows.anchor: Bu hitap mücrimlere mahsustur. Zira sabır ile ecre veya terfî‘-i dereceye mazhar edilmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God pardons many of people's sins instead of punishing them in this world, as 35:45 confirms.
rows.anchor: Hâlbuki birçoğundan af buyuruyor yani kesbettiğiniz günahlarınızın birçoğundan af buyuruyor da dünyada muâhaze etmiyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No matter what strength people gain, they cannot escape on earth the calamities destined to reach them.
rows.anchor: siz ne olsanız bu Arz’dasınız ve her ne yaparsanız, ne kuvvetler iktisab etseniz başınıza gelmesi mukadder olan musibetlerden yakanızı kurtaramazsınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People have no protector or helper apart from God.
rows.anchor: sizin için Allah’tan başka ne re’sen kurtaracak bir velî, bir hâmi vardır, ne de yardım edip def‘edecek bir nasîr.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thus protection comes through seeking refuge in God and carrying out one's duties according to His commands and laws.
rows.anchor: Allah’a sığınıp O’nun emirlerine, kanunlarına göre vazife îfâ etmekten başka suretle korunmanın çaresi yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ships like mountains crossing the sea illustrate that people's earthly condition is like that of those aboard a ship.
rows.anchor: denizde akan dağlar gibi gemiler sizin de Arz’da hâliniz o gemidekilerin hâli gibidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wind is the moving force that drives ships; if God stops it, the ships remain motionless on the sea.
rows.anchor: dilerse o rüzgârı, yani o gemileri hareket ettiren kuvve-i muharrikeyi durduruverir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The still ships are signs for the patient and grateful, proving human helplessness and that only God can protect or help.
rows.anchor: çok sabırlı, çok şükreden her kimse için birçok[^2] âyetler vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The impatient fail to board and contemplate these events; the ungrateful fail to value reflection and draw its conclusions, hence the saying that half of faith is patience and half is gratitude.
rows.anchor: sabrı olmayanlar bu gemilere binip de bu vukū‘âtı müşahede ve tefekküre himmet edemezler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A saying divides faith into two halves: patience and gratitude.
rows.anchor: onun için demişlerdir ki imanın nısfı sabır, nısfı şükürdür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb ʿasha denotes weakness of sight, such as night blindness; here it means deliberately acting blind and refusing to see.
rows.anchor: “Aşâ” gözde bir nevi zaaf ve “tavuk karanlığı” tâbir olunan görmemezlik, bir nevi körlük.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The remembrance of the All-Merciful” means the Qur'an; whoever turns away from it refuses its guidance, as Quraysh did.
rows.anchor: Rahmân’ın zikri Kur’an, yani her kim Kur’an’dan göz yumup görmemezlik eder, onun irşâdını dinlemezse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As an example of Quraysh's rejection, he says they asked why this Qur'an had not been revealed, leaving the quotation unfinished.
rows.anchor: Kureyş böyle yapmışlardı هَٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانُ لَوْلَا نُزِّلَ ilh… demişlerdi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh undervalued the Prophet because he lacked worldly wealth, as Pharaoh boasted of Egypt against Moses; this story consoles and strengthens the Prophet and warns his opponents.
rows.anchor: Firavun da Hazret-i Mûsâ’ya karşı أَلَيْسَ لِى مُلْكُ مِصْرَ diye öyle gururlanmıştı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage also answers the command to ask those sent before, so its main purpose is to establish that answer rather than merely repeat the story.
rows.anchor: Bir de وَسْـَٔلْ مَنْ أَرْسَلْنَا suâli üzerine bir cevâbı dahi tazammun eder. Binâen‘aleyh asıl maksat kıssanın tekrarı değil, bu cevapların takrîridir[^1].

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story also contains subtleties not found in its tellings elsewhere.
rows.anchor: Bununla beraber nefs-i kıssada da diğer yerlerde bulunmayan nükteler dahi eksik değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation of jāthiya is “kneeling”; the author says the intended implication is the composed, careful, respectful posture of kneeling.
rows.anchor: Birisi diz çökmüş mânasına ki lâzımı muraddır. Zira diz çökmek derli toplu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation takes jāthiya to mean a gathered assembly, deriving it from jathwa, a heap of stones.
rows.anchor: Birisi de toplanmış cemaat mânasınadır ki جثوه’den me’huzdur. Bir araya gelmiş taş yığınına denir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intended scene is every community assembled before God for reckoning, as described in 36:32.
rows.anchor: Murad, Sûre-i Yâsîn’de وَإِن كُلٌّۭ لَّمَّا جَمِيعٌۭ لَّدَيْنَا مُحْضَرُونَ [36/32] buyurulduğu üzere Hakk’ın huzûrunda hesap için toplanmaktır.
